title: Partition Labels
spaceBreakdown:
- int last[26]: fixed 26 entries → O(1)
- vector<int> result: returned output → not counted
- recursion depth: none
approach: A partition containing character `c` must extend at least to the last position where `c` appears, otherwise `c` would leak into a later part. In a first pass, record `last[c]` for every character. Then scan left to right, maintaining the current partition's required end as the running maximum of `last[s[i]]` over all characters seen so far in the partition. When the scan reaches that end, every character inside has all its occurrences contained, so we can safely cut - and cutting as early as possible maximizes the number of parts.
hints: Look at the first partition in Example 1, "ababcbaca" - what is true about the last position of every letter inside it, compared to the rest of the string?
Use a fixed array `last[26]` storing the final index of each letter. In Example 1, `last['a'] = 8`, so any partition containing `'a'` must extend at least to index 8.

**Single character** - n = 1, only one partition is possible.
`Input: s = "a"` → `Expected: [1]`
⚠️ Bug: computing size as `end - start` instead of `end - start + 1` → returns `[0]`.

**Non-contiguous character occurrences** - a letter appears at two distant positions.
`Input: s = "abac"` → `Expected: [4]`
⚠️ Bug: closing when `last[s[i]-'a'] == i` instead of tracking the running max `end` → returns `[2, 1, 1]`, splitting `'a'` across the first and second partitions.

**Entire string is one partition** - every character's range overlaps with another's.
`Input: s = "abacbd"` → `Expected: [5, 1]`
⚠️ Bug: setting `end = last[s[start]-'a']` only once at partition start and never updating it during the scan → returns `[3, 1, 1, 1]`, splitting `'b'` across partitions.

**Boundary: last character** - the final partition closes exactly at index n−1.
`Input: s = "ababcbacadefegdehijhklij"` → `Expected: [9, 7, 8]`
⚠️ Bug: loop condition `i < n - 1` instead of `i < n` → never closes the last partition, returns `[9, 7]`.

followUps.q: What if `s` contains any Unicode character, not just lowercase English letters?
followUps.a: Replace the fixed `int last[26]` array with a hash map keyed by the character. The algorithm is unchanged: two passes, O(n) time, O(min(n, |Σ|)) space where |Σ| is the alphabet size.

followUps.q: What if each partition must also contain at most `k` distinct characters?
followUps.a: While expanding the current partition, track the set of distinct characters seen so far; when the next character would push the count above `k`, close the partition before it. Still O(n) time, O(|Σ|) space for the last-occurrence map plus O(k) for the distinct-character set.

followUps.q: What if `s` arrives as a single-pass stream and you cannot store the whole string?
followUps.a: You cannot solve it exactly in one pass, because a partition's end depends on the last occurrence of every character inside it, which may appear later in the stream. You need a first pass to record last occurrences, then a second pass to emit partitions - so exact solving requires O(|Σ|) metadata and the ability to re-read the input.
